subject: history
title: Viceroys of India and Their Contributions
description: List of Viceroys from Canning to Mountbatten with key events during their tenure

content.overview: The Viceroy was the representative of the British Crown in India. Here are the major Viceroys and their contributions.
keyPoints: Lord Canning (1856-1862): First Viceroy, Revolt of 1857, Government of India Act 1858
Lord Mayo (1869-1872): First census (1872), Mayo College established
Lord Lytton (1876-1880): Vernacular Press Act, Arms Act, Delhi Durbar 1877, Great Famine
Lord Ripon (1880-1884): Ilbert Bill, Local Self-Government, Factories Act, first census
Lord Dufferin (1884-1888): Third Burmese War, INC founded (1885)
Lord Lansdowne (1888-1894): Indian Councils Act 1892,Factories Act
Lord Curzon (1899-1905): Partition of Bengal (1905), Curzon-Kitchener controversy, Ancient Monuments Act
Lord Minto (1905-1910): Morley-Minto Reforms (1909), Muslim League founded (1906)
Lord Hardinge (1910-1916): Capital shifted to Delhi (1911), Delhi Durbar
Lord Chelmsford (1916-1921): Rowlatt Act, Jallianwala Bagh, Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms
Lord Reading (1921-1926): Chauri Caura, RSS founded (1925)
Lord Irwin (1926-1931): Simon Commission, Dandi March, Gandhi-Irwin Pact
Lord Willingdon (1931-1936): Poona Pact, Government of India Act 1935
Lord Linlithgow (1936-1943): WWII, Cripps Mission, Quit India Movement
Lord Wavell (1943-1947): Wavell Plan, Shimla Conference
Lord Mountbatten (1947): Last Viceroy, Independence and Partition

mnemonics.trick: C-M-L-R-D-M-C-H-R-I-W-L-W-M = Canning, Mayo, Lytton, Ripon, Dufferin, Minto, Curzon, Hardinge, Reading, Irwin, Willingdon, Linlithgow, Wavell, Mountbatten
mnemonics.explanation: Remember the order: Canning, Mayo, Lytton, Ripon, Dufferin, Minto, Curzon, Hardinge, Reading, Irwin, Willingdon, Linlithgow, Wavell, Mountbatten

quiz.question: Who was the first Viceroy of India?
quiz.explanation: Lord Canning was the first Viceroy of India (1856-1862)

quiz.question: Partition of Bengal was done by:
Who was the last Viceroy of India?
quiz.explanation: Lord Mountbatten was the last Viceroy of India (1947)
